title: Signature Counterexample Provenance
description: Signature edition: every counterexample records what it refutes — the exact claim, version, and context — plus its full minimization history. When the claim changes, affected counterexamples are re-evaluated automatically; the refutation stays attached to the right claim version. This is a Signature original method.
method: Bind counterexamples to (claim, version); re-evaluate on claim change; keep the minimization history.
usage: Re-evaluate bound counterexamples when claims change; retire refuted claims' counterexamples deliberately.

demo.code:
print('counterexample #77 bound to claim v3')
print('claim -> v4: re-evaluated -> still refutes (kept) / resolved (retired)')

title: Signature Fuzzing for counterexamples
description: Signature edition: Property-based fuzzers generate counterexamples by search: Hypothesis finds the input breaking your invariant, often one no human would construct. Fuzzing-derived counterexamples come with replay scripts — the violation is executable, not theoretical.
method: State the property; fuzz with structure-aware generation; on violation, capture the input; shrink it; emit a replay test.
usage: Write properties first; let the fuzzer hunt; keep every found counterexample as a regression test.

title: Signature Adversarial example generation (ML)
description: Signature edition: For ML models, counterexamples are adversarial inputs: tiny perturbations flipping the prediction. Generators (FGSM, PGD) systematically find them, and each one refutes the claim 'the model is robust here'. Adversarial counterexamples drove the entire robustness research program.
method: Gradient-guided perturbation within an epsilon ball; verify the prediction flips; the perturbed input is the counterexample.
usage: Generate adversarially during training (adversarial training); test robustness on held-out attacks.

demo.code:
print('image classified "panda" (99%); PGD epsilon=0.03 -> "gibbon" (87%)')
print('counterexample: imperceptible perturbation flips prediction')

title: Signature Mutation-driven counterexamples
description: Signature edition: Mutate the program slightly and check whether the property still holds: surviving mutants are counterexamples to the claim 'the tests verify the property'. Each surviving mutant is a concrete program variant your verification misses — a gap made tangible.
method: Generate mutants; check the property per mutant; survivors are verification gaps; strengthen the property or tests.
usage: Treat surviving mutants as counterexamples to your verification, not just your tests.

demo.code:
print('mutant: > changed to >= in bounds check')
print('property still "holds" -> SURVIVED: verification gap (off-by-one not caught)')

title: Signature Witness generation for liveness
description: Signature edition: Liveness violations ('something good eventually happens') need infinite counterexamples — lassos (a stem plus a cycle avoiding the good thing). Generators produce the lasso: the finite representation of 'never'. It's the counterexample shape for progress properties.
method: Search for lassos avoiding the desired state; the (stem, cycle) pair is the violation; present it as 'repeats forever without progress'.
usage: Read liveness counterexamples as 'this cycle repeats forever'; the fix breaks the cycle.

demo.code:
print('liveness: every request eventually granted')
print('lasso: request -> retry -> request -> retry ... (grant never occurs)')

title: Signature Counterexample databases
description: Signature edition: Counterexamples are assets: a database of past counterexamples (with the bug, the fix, and the regression test) turns one team's found bug into every team's avoided bug. New code is checked against the historical counterexample corpus automatically.
method: Archive (counterexample, bug, fix, test); check new code against the corpus; the corpus grows with every found bug.
usage: Archive every significant counterexample; make the corpus check part of CI.

demo.code:
print('corpus: 1,204 counterexamples archived')
print('new parser checked vs corpus: 3 historical patterns matched -> flagged pre-merge')

title: Signature TLC minimal traces
description: Signature edition: TLC reports the shortest trace to a violation — the minimal sequence of states from init to bug. Minimal traces are debuggable traces: every step matters, and the design flaw is usually obvious at the step where the invariant first breaks.
method: Model check; on violation, extract the minimal trace; walk it step by step; find where the design went wrong.
usage: Walk the trace from the start; the bug is at the first surprising step.

demo.code:
print('TLC: invariant violated at state 7 of 7-step trace')
print('step 4: second leader elected -> design flaw: election not fenced')

title: Signature Delta debugging and shrinking
description: Signature edition: A 10MB crashing input is useless; delta debugging (ddmin) and shrinkers reduce it to the minimal failing case automatically. The minimal counterexample is the debuggable one — shrinking turns 'it breaks on this huge input' into 'it breaks on [1]'.
method: Take the failing input; repeatedly try smaller variants; keep those that still fail; converge on the minimal case.
usage: Always shrink before triaging; the minimal case usually reveals the bug's shape.

demo.code:
failing = [3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9, 2, 6]
print('original failing input:', failing)
print('shrunk: [1] (minimal case preserving failure)')

title: Signature Alloy instance generation
description: Signature edition: Alloy's analyzer doesn't just say 'no' — it shows a concrete instance violating the assertion, rendered as a diagram. Counterexamples as pictures: the design flaw is visible, not just logical. It's the most humane counterexample generator in formal methods.
method: Write the model and assertion; the analyzer produces a counterexample instance within scope; visualize and inspect.
usage: Inspect counterexamples visually; they're design feedback, not just failures.

demo.code:
print('assertion: no orphaned files')
print('counterexample: [File F1] --no owner--> (diagram shown)')
print('design fix: require owner on creation')
